about: The one world-history dataset in Prometheus (owner, 2026-11-24: Athenaeum's world history, refined and expanded, used by every pillar; denser for recent centuries). Every entry: a date and its precision, a title and one-paragraph text, the regions and themes it touches, a place, its sources with the page's own words, who found it and whether it is checked. Edit this file, then run tools/history/build.py: it checks every entry and writes world-history.js (any page) and cause-event-consequence.json (Athenaeum's chronicle).

notes: Each entry: cause → event → consequence, analytical; the one-line source is the Wikipedia article opened 2026-11-10 (API extract).
evidence_quotes are exact substrings of the opened article text (machine-checked: 0 misses), so every causal claim is traceable.
Wikipedia is a tertiary source; for citation in writing, follow its references.

2026-11-24: each entry's place, coordinates and exact span from Gemini ATH-GEM-06 (athenaeum_gemini_history-dates_20261124-0023.json); the written date stays the one the chronicle orders by (Sakoku's span is its forced end, 1853-54).

entries.title: Late Bronze Age collapse
entries.text: Late Bronze Age collapse of palace-centred states.

chain.cause: Interlinked palace economies of the Aegean, Anatolia and Levant came under combined stresses (proposed: climate change, volcanic activity, drought, violent destruction of cities).
chain.event: Late Bronze Age collapse of palace-centred states.
chain.consequence: Mycenaean palace economy fragmented into isolated villages (Greek Dark Ages); the Hittite Empire fell; Egypt and Assyria survived weakened; Phoenicians gained autonomy.

entries.text: British–French–Israeli invasion of Egypt.

chain.cause: Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal; an Egyptian blockade restricted Israeli passage.
chain.event: British–French–Israeli invasion of Egypt.
chain.consequence: US, Soviet and UN pressure forced withdrawal, showing the UK and France could no longer act without US consent.

sources.quote: which Nasser had nationalised earlier that year

entries.by: Grok (10 Nov chronicle pack); dates and places Gemini ATH-GEM-06
entries.note: Crisis began July 1956 and invasion occurred October–November 1956; Israeli troops withdrew in March 1957.
quotes: which Nasser had nationalised earlier that year
prompting their withdrawal from Egypt
could no longer implement independent foreign policies without U.S. consent

entries.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
entries.text: 13-day confrontation, the closest the Cold War came to full nuclear war.

chain.cause: US nuclear missiles in the UK, Italy and Turkey were matched by Soviet missile deployments in Cuba.
chain.event: 13-day confrontation, the closest the Cold War came to full nuclear war.
chain.consequence: Creation of the Moscow–Washington hotline and later agreements that reduced tensions.

entries.title: 1973 oil embargo
entries.text: Oil embargo and price shock (about $3 to nearly $12/barrel).

chain.cause: OAPEC embargoed countries that supported Israel in the Yom Kippur War.
chain.event: Oil embargo and price shock (about $3 to nearly $12/barrel).
chain.consequence: US policy response: 55 mph limit, CAFE fuel-economy standards, Strategic Petroleum Reserve, Department of Energy.

sources.quote: implementing a total oil embargo against countries that had supported Israel

entries.by: Grok (10 Nov chronicle pack); dates and places Gemini ATH-GEM-06
entries.note: Embargo began in October 1973 and was lifted in March 1974.
quotes: implementing a total oil embargo against countries that had supported Israel
from US$3/barrel to nearly US$12/barrel
Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards

entries.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
entries.text: Crowds crossed the Berlin border on 9 November 1989.

chain.cause: Revolutions of 1989 (Hungary opened its border) and a Politburo press conference prematurely announcing unrestricted travel.
chain.event: Crowds crossed the Berlin border on 9 November 1989.
chain.consequence: Free elections favoured reunification; Germany reunified on 3 October 1990.
